#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Device Plugins that wish to leverage the Topology Manager can send back a populated TopologyInfo struct as part of the device registration, along with the device IDs and the health of the device. TopologyInfo is converted to TopologyHints and used by TopologyManager to find the optimal/desired resource allocation for a Pod.

If a plugin sends an empty but non-nil instance of TopologyInfo for a resource, devicemanager passes it on as an empty instance of TopologyHint which is currently interpreted as "Hint Provider has no possible NUMA affinities for resource" which further means that pods requesting that resource will fail.

To not block device resources that pass TopologyInfo{Nodes:[]*NUMANode{}} from being used, interprete that as nil set of hints and not a []TopologyHint{}.

issue_context.title: TopologyManager fails a Pod with AffinityError
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

A node with:

```
$ sudo grep ^topolo /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml
topologyManager: true
topologyManagerPolicy: single-numa-node 
```

fails a pod that uses device plugin resources (empty but non-nil `TopologyHints`) :

```
...
Sep 05 00:35:14 node kubelet[1468778]: I0905 00:35:14.935079 1468778 server.go:142] "Got registration request from device plugin with resource" resourceName="sgx.intel.com/enclave"
Sep 05 00:35:14 node kubelet[1468778]: I0905 00:35:14.935212 1468778 handler.go:94] "Registered client" name="sgx.intel.com/enclave"
Sep 05 00:35:14 node kubelet[1468778]: I0905 00:35:14.939947 1468778 client.go:86] "State pushed for device plugin" resource="sgx.intel.com/enclave" resourceCapacity=0
Sep 05 00:35:14 node kubelet[1468778]: I0905 00:35:14.945504 1468778 client.go:86] "State pushed for device plugin" resource="sgx.intel.com/enclave" resourceCapacity=1
Sep 05 00:35:15 node kubelet[1468778]: I0905 00:35:15.429131 1468778 setters.go:310] "Updated capacity for device plugin" plugin="sgx.intel.com/enclave" capacity=1
...
...
Sep 05 00:40:55 node kubelet[1468778]: I0905 00:40:55.907739 1468778 scope_container.go:77] "TopologyHints" hints=map[sgx.intel.com/enclave:[]] pod="default/intelsgx-demo-job-m2r56" containerName="intelsgx-demo-job-1"
Sep 05 00:40:55 node kubelet[1468778]: I0905 00:40:55.907929 1468778 policy.go:86] "Hint Provider has no possible NUMA affinities for resource" resource="sgx.intel.com/enclave"
```

Our device plugin sends the following registration:
```
I0905 00:35:14.939438 1474973 server.go:106] Sending to kubelet[&Device{ID:sgx-enclave-0,Health:Healthy,Topology:&TopologyInfo{Nodes:[]*NUMANode{},},}]
```

So we send an empty `TopologyInfo` which is interpreted as "no possible NUMA affinities":
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bcea98234f0fdc5ce4e976758977eec72b13bfd4/pkg/kubelet/cm/topologymanager/policy.go#L85-L89

How is this different from `nil` value?
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bcea98234f0fdc5ce4e976758977eec72b13bfd4/pkg/kubelet/cm/topologymanager/policy.go#L79-L83

### What did you expect to happen?

I can workaround the problem by sending `TopologyInfo: nil` but it's not [well documented](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/extend-kubernetes/compute-storage-net/device-plugins/#device-plugin-integration-with-the-topology-manager) how this is supposed to work. Can the two if's combined or should we updated the documentation?

My environment: a single-node k8s cluster w/ device plugin that does

The node needs to run two kinds of pods: those that need/use topology single-numa-node  and pods that just use a device plugin resources that does not provide topologyhints.

It's possible that better documentation is needed, but we could also probably do more to handle this better in the device plugin.

The implementation you pointed out above relies on `nil` depicting "don't care" and `[]TopologyHint{}` depicting "I tried but couldn't generate any hints that provide alignment". 

One could argue though that `TopologyInfo{Nodes:[]*NUMANode{}}` should have generated a `nil` set of hints and not a `[]TopologyHint{}`. I would need to look at the code again to know for sure if this makes sense or not though.

> The implementation you pointed out above relies on `nil` depicting "don't care" and `[]TopologyHint{}` depicting "I tried but couldn't generate any hints that provide alignment".

This interpretation makes sense but

> One could argue though that `TopologyInfo{Nodes:[]*NUMANode{}}` should have generated a `nil` set of hints and not a `[]TopologyHint{}`.

Right, if the hint provider fails to provide hints, I guess the pod should not be blamed (by not making it to run) for that.

/sig node
I can at least help with the documentation part if we decide that it alone needs changing.

> /cc @fromanirh @swatisehgal

I'm reviewing this area for other reasons, we should indeed calrify the hint API expectations. Up until now my rule of thumb was pretty much "what cpumanager does" which has room for improvement.

This could be isolated to `devicemanager` only by  returning `true` when `!= nil && len() > 0`:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cae4c036c872b340e5eabbf7eb1593640517aa22/pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/topology_hints.go#L142

when `len() == 0` running `generateDeviceTopologyHints()` is pointless, IMO
